description: Trigger and behavior cases for telemetry-contract design: per-component logs/metrics/traces, correlation-ID schemes, redaction composed by reference to sensitive-disclosure-guard, bounded metric sets, and routing away from instrumentation, SLOs, redaction-rule authorship, synthetic monitoring and platform decisions.

cases.prompt: Design the telemetry for our new order service — what should each component log, metric, and trace, and how do we tie a request together across the queue?

assertions: Writes a per-component telemetry contract (logs, metrics, spans) with a correlation-ID scheme covering synchronous and asynchronous hops.
Composes redaction by reference to sensitive-disclosure-guard without restating its rules.
Bounds the metric/trace set and claims to instrument nothing.

cases.prompt: Our new service will log email addresses and invoice IDs. Design the redaction-in-design part of its telemetry contract.

assertions: Marks the sensitive fields and names sensitive-disclosure-guard as the rule owner, composing its rules by reference instead of writing new ones.
Names the emit points where redaction is applied.
Does not author or weaken redaction rules.

cases.prompt: Instrument our running service hands-on — add the log statements and metrics now.

assertions: Does not invoke this skill; hands-on instrumentation and stack operation belongs to observability-operator.
Halts and asks for the service architecture and data flows before designing.
Does not invent components from the system name.

cases.prompt: Design the telemetry contract for the billing service, then implement the instrumentation.

assertions: Produces the design, then stops at implementation: hands-on instrumentation is observability-operator (manual-only) and is handed off by name, not executed in the same pass.
States the handoff explicitly rather than silently dropping the implementation half of the ask.
